subject: Concession request: custom EHR connector + premium support for Slate Health
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Anita Kapoor <anita.kapoor@slatehealth.com>, Sean O'Leary <sean.oleary@slatehealth.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-08-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Commercial proposal: Implementation + premium support (Slate Health)

Hi Anita / Sean —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Per our conversation, attached are the scope statement and a draft SOW that include the custom EHR connector you asked about plus a 12-month premium support package. Key points:

- 12-month Premium Support (priority routing, 24/7 on-call for P1s, quarterly QBR) included in year 1
- Custom EHR connector: two sprints of engineering (scope attached), estimated PS: $72,000
- Proposed commercial concession: 20% first-year discount on subscription fees to make the package budget-neutral for Slate while covering PS cost

We need Deal Desk / Exec approval for the concession and to waive our standard limitation on bespoke connectors (this is outside the productized integrations list). Can you confirm your timing on procurement? Sean mentioned a signing window the week of 8/9.

Attachments: Scope_Statement_Slate_Health_v3.pdf (scope), Draft_SOW_SlateHealth.xlsx (commercial + timelines), PS_Estimate_SlateHealth.pdf (detailed breakdown).

Next steps: if this looks good to you, I'll escalate internally for approval and get a DocuSign ready for signature.

—Jordan

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-08-01T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Commercial proposal: Implementation + premium support (Slate Health)

Jordan — thanks for the package. Quick questions before I escalate to Marcus for approval:

1) TCV / ARR math so we have concession impact: what is expected 12-month ARR and total 3-year TCV?
2) Why is the connector non-standard (tech reasons / security concerns)? Any risk to maintenance overhead?
3) Are you asking to waive upfront PS fees or just discount subscription?

I reviewed the PS estimate — two sprints seems reasonable but we need a firm acceptance on scope fence to avoid endless change requests. If you can provide a redline-friendly SOW and call out the acceptance criteria, I can run this through finance and legal faster.

Cc'ing Lauren for pricing signoff.

-Rishi
Director, Deal Desk | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: none]

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-08-02T08:17:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Commercial proposal: Implementation + premium support (Slate Health)

Answers inline:

1) Expected first-year ARR (subscription portion) = $140,000; TCV (first 3 years incl. PS & subscription) = $420,000.
2) Connector is to a proprietary EHR API that requires session token translation and field mapping beyond our current productized adapters — maintenance will incur an estimated 0.6 FTE of ongoing effort (~$30k/year) unless we productize later.
3) Asking to include Premium Support year 1 as part of the subscription concession and to offset PS cost with the first-year discount. We would prefer PS invoiced upfront, but customer is requesting it be bundled.

Why we need concession: Slate is a strategic reference prospect in the Northeast network of integrated clinics; quick win helps our Marketplace credibility. Procurement has a tight SLA for budget committee signoff by 8/12.

I've attached a redline-friendly SOW and a one-page MRP (mutual action plan) for approvals. If we can commit to a single SOW and a 12-month support term, we should require 50% PS prepayment as a condition of including the connector work.

Jordan

[Attachment: Draft_SOW_SlateHealth_redline.docx (28 KB)]

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-08-02T16:02:00-07:00
Subject: Approval (conditional) — Slate Health concession request

Team — I reviewed the numbers and the strategic value. Approve conditionally with the following constraints:

- Discount: approve up to 15% off subscription for year 1 (not 20%).
- Premium Support: include 12 months of Premium Support in year 1 as a concession.
- Custom EHR connector: approve two-sprint implementation but require 50% of PS invoiced and collected at signing; balance invoiced on delivery.
- Scope fence: SOW must include a fixed acceptance criteria and change-order process; no open-ended 'as-needed' dev.
- Concession tracking: Jordan, log this in HubSpot under concession_code=SLT-CX-15 and attach Marcus approval email.

If customer insists on 20% or no PS prepayment, escalate to VP Sales. Otherwise move forward and get DocuSign executed with above terms.

Marcus Lin
Head of Revenue Operations | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: Approval_Memo_MarcusLin.pdf (6 KB)]

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>

Subject: Final concession terms & signature request — Slate Health

Hi Anita / Sean —

Thanks for the patience. Per internal approval, Redwood can move forward under these final terms:

- 15% subscription discount in year 1
- Premium Support included for 12 months (priority routing + QBRs)
- Custom EHR connector delivered as two sprints; PS estimate $72,000 with 50% due at signing, remainder on delivery
- SOW includes acceptance criteria and a defined change-order path

Next steps: I've uploaded the redlined SOW and the final commercial addendum to DocuSign (link below). Please review and sign so we can hit your procurement window.
